inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026) consolidated net sales, JPY bn-scale in millions: 1,307,560. Company labels this year 'FY25'; the repo labels it FY2026. Year 1 of the projection is the year ending March 2027 (company 'FY26'), for which guidance exists.
inputs.share_count_basis: 706,669,170 issued less 3,172,718 treasury (incl. BBT trust shares) at 30 June 2026 = 703,496,452, post 10-for-1 split of 1 July 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin). No dilutive securities (diluted EPS reported as nil). Held FLAT: SBC is nil, no convertible or equity-raise programme announced.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net interest-bearing debt JPY 292.1bn at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 presentation B/S summary, up from 247.5bn at March 2026 on the capex/working-capital build). Cash and deposits 60.7bn; gross interest-bearing debt derived as 352.8bn. The company figure excludes lease liabilities (~12.5bn at March 2024), which is consistent with lease treatment (B) below. Post balance date: UACJ stake sold Sept 2026 for ~28.3bn cash (gain ~21.7bn), which moves value from the securities bridge item into cash -- neutral to equity value, not double counted.
inputs.sbc_source: J-GAAP filer; equity compensation is limited to a Board Benefit Trust for directors, not separately disclosed in the tanshin and immaterial (<0.05% of revenue). Treated as an SBC-zero market per owner-fcf-adaptations (e): SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house and street bases coincide, band_position collapses.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income JPY 1,875m in FY2024 (Integrated Report 2024 p.91, latest full P&L in the extracted filings); FY2026 figure not in the tanshin summary. Stripped from the FCF base because cash (60.7bn) is netted against gross debt in the bridge. Dividend income (~1.2bn) and equity-method profit (16.5bn FY2026) are likewise excluded from the component build, which starts from operating profit -- their source assets are carried in equity_bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: No share repurchases in the period; the flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for, but with SBC at zero there is no dilution to fund.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows: 10y JGB ~1.7% risk-free, 6.0% ERP, equity beta ~1.3-1.4 for a cyclical cable/optical manufacturer currently traded as an AI-infrastructure proxy -> cost of equity ~9.8-10.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~1.2% (JPY bonds and bank loans), 0.85% after tax; weights ~85/15 equity/debt at market value (market cap ~JPY 1.97tn vs gross debt 0.35tn) -> WACC ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. Within the house reference of ~9% for JPY industrials. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and the data-center dependency are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (adaptations f).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Lease liability repayments (~JPY 2.8bn/yr, IFRS-subsidiary leases, FY2024 cash flow statement) plus ~0.3bn lease interest are charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.25% of revenue; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt (the company's net interest-bearing debt already excludes them). The parent is J-GAAP and expenses operating leases, so no further adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests deducted once in the bridge at book (JPY 18.0bn at 30 June 2026). NCI fell from 32.3bn to 18.2bn in FY2026 when Furukawa Battery was deconsolidated, so the remaining NCI profit share (~0.8bn/quarter) is small relative to group profit.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (routing table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Furukawa Electric is a diversified cable / optical fiber / electronic-materials manufacturer, not a bank, REIT, LIC or holdco; its value is an operating cash-flow stream, so no other model applies. Cyclical adaptations applied: JPY WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for investment securities and equity-method affiliates (income excluded from flows, assets added to bridge with a haircut), SBC-zero (band_position null). Peak-earnings handling: FY2026 (and the FY2027 guidance year) are a cycle high driven by AI data-center optical/thermal demand and a 31% higher copper price; the base case holds the guided margin for the capex-build years then fades the EBITDA margin to a mid-cycle 10.5% (operating margin ~6%, roughly midway between the prior-cycle best of 4.6% and the 8.0% guided / 10%+ Vision 2030 target), rather than extrapolating FY2027. Historical owner FCF is negative in 8 of the last 12 years (cumulative reported FCF 2015-2026 about -JPY 93bn), so the valuation rests entirely on the post-capex-wave cash generation, which is why the bear case lands near zero and carries 25% weight. 'FY' labels: the company calls the year ending March 2027 'FY26'; this file uses the repo convention (FY2027).

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities and equity-method investments (est. JPY 145bn at 30 Jun 2026, less 20% for deferred tax on unrealised gains)
equity_bridge.note: Investments and other assets 189.8bn at Jun 2026 (Q1 FY2027 presentation) less ~45bn of deferred tax, retirement-benefit and other assets. Reconciles from the March 2024 audited 131.7bn: -32.9bn UACJ reclassification/sale (FY2025), +35bn (FY2026), +~21bn (Q1 FY2027, mostly mark-to-market). Added because equity-method profit (16.5bn FY2026) and dividend income are excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule, adaptations d). UACJ ~28.3bn was converted to cash in Sept 2026, after the balance-sheet date.
Q1 FY2027 presentation B/S summary; charged once here, flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (66% / 49%) diverge far more than 30% from the equity CAGRs (11% / 10%) because FY2023 and FY2021 were trough years and FY2026 EPS includes JPY 29.1bn of extraordinary income (retirement-plan revision gain); they are not a usable forward proxy. Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: owner FCF was negative in FY2021-FY2024 and FY2026 (reported FCF -40.4, -51.4, -7.3, -7.1, +21.2, -28.6bn). Revenue 3yr CAGR selected; note ~JPY 50bn of the FY2026 revenue increase was copper-price and FX pass-through, so underlying volume growth is lower.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs from metrics_normalized: revenue FY2023 1,066,326 -> FY2026 1,307,560 (3yr) and FY2021 811,600 -> FY2026 (5yr); equity 301,859 -> 417,048 and 260,076 -> 417,048; EPS 22.58 -> 103.02 and 14.19 -> 103.02 (post-split basis). SBC is nil so the owner-FCF series equals reported FCF less interest income; the adjustment does not change the (negative) CAGR picture.

base.growth_note: Year 1 = FY2027 guidance of JPY 1,530bn (+17.0%, raised 6 Aug 2026; Q1 ran +24% with copper at 2,220/kg and USD/JPY 160). Years 2-3 carry the data-center build (new water-cooled module, DFB laser and HVDC capacity coming on stream) at 9% and 7%, then decelerate to Japanese nominal GDP-like 2.5% by year 7. Year-5 revenue ~JPY 1.95tn vs the ~2.4-2.5tn implied by Vision 2030's OP 250bn at 10%+.
base.margin_note: EBITDA = operating profit + D&A, before the 0.25% lease charge. Year 1 at 11.0% gives operating profit ~JPY 118bn (7.75%) vs the 123bn / 8.0% guided -- a ~4% haircut for the Middle East resin/transport cost impact management explicitly left out of guidance. Peaks at 12.0% in year 3 as the capex comes on stream, then fades to 10.5% (operating margin ~6.0% after 4.3% D&A and the lease charge). Mid-cycle reference points: FY2017-FY2026 EBITDA margin averaged 6.2% with a pre-boom best of 7.3%; FY2027 guidance 11.0%; Vision 2030 10%+ operating margin (~14% EBITDA). 10.5% credits the structural mix shift (data-center optics/thermal from ~15% to ~45% of profit, exits from batteries, magnet wire and the UACJ stake) at roughly half of management's target.
base.capex_da_note: Capex JPY 150bn guided for FY2027 (9.8% of sales; ~45bn heat-dissipation/cooling, ~16bn HVDC, ~7bn DFB laser) vs 56.7bn in FY2026; assumed to stay elevated at 7.5% and 6.0% for two more years of the Vision 2030 programme before settling at 4.5% (10-yr history 3.2-5.8%, mean ~4.3%). D&A guided 46bn (3.0%) in FY2027 and rises to 4.3% as the new plant depreciates; terminal capex slightly above D&A for 2% growth.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer with receivables + inventories (~JPY 515bn at Jun 2026) well above trade payables: growth consumes cash. FY2026 absorbed 54bn of working capital on 106bn of revenue growth (copper-inflated); -20% of incremental revenue is the structural rate used.
base.tax_note: Japanese statutory ~30.6%; FY2026 effective 27.6%; cash taxes paid 11.1bn in FY2024. 30% flat, no loss carryforwards of note.
base.terminal_note: Cap at 14x owner FCF (cyclical, per method: 12-15x) -- equivalent to ~11-12x terminal NOPAT. Gordon at 8.5%/2.0% would be 15.7x, so the cap binds.

bull.narrative: Vision 2030 delivered: revenue ~JPY 2.27tn and EBITDA 15% (operating profit ~JPY 245bn, 10.8%) in FY2031, i.e. the company's own OP 250bn / 10%+ target, with the AI data-center optical and cooling demand continuing through 2028-2030 and the 150bn capex programme earning its return. Margins then fade only to 13% as the mix stays data-center weighted.

bear.narrative: Hyperscaler capex digestion from FY2029 (the 2001-2002 optical pattern: Furukawa bought OFS at the peak and spent a decade recovering), copper retreats from 2,200/kg, Chinese harness competition keeps Automotive Systems margins falling. Revenue -6% / -2% in years 3-4; EBITDA margin reverts to 8% -- still above the FY2017-2026 average of 6.2% because the battery and magnet-wire exits are permanent -- but the FY2027-28 capex wave leaves D&A at 4.2-4.6% of sales, so operating margin settles near 3.5%, close to the prior-cycle years. With JPY 292bn of net debt, equity value on this path is close to zero.

scenario_narratives.base: AI data-center demand for optical fiber/cable, MT ferrules, DFB lasers, copper foil and water-cooled thermal modules carries FY2027 to guidance (sales +17%, OP ~JPY 118-123bn) and two more years of 9%/7% growth while the JPY 150bn capex programme comes on stream; margins peak at 12% EBITDA in FY2029 and fade to a 10.5% mid-cycle (operating margin ~6%) as the hyperscaler cycle normalises and the new capacity depreciates. Energy Infrastructure (HVDC, submarine cable) and Metal Solutions grow with Japanese grid renewal; Automotive Systems stays a low-margin drag. Working capital and capex absorb nearly all cash until FY2029; free cash flow only turns meaningfully positive from year 3, so the value is terminal-heavy. Credits roughly half of the Vision 2030 OP 250bn target.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vision 2030 is delivered: data-center products (targeted at ~80% of incremental profit) take Optical Solutions and Digital Infrastructure Components to a combined OP well above JPY 150bn by FY2030, revenue compounds at 20/14/11/8/6% and EBITDA reaches 15% in FY2031 (OP ~JPY 245bn, 10.8%). Capacity added in FY2027-FY2029 is sold out as fiber and cooling-component supply stays tight; margins fade only to 13% as the mix stays data-center weighted. Portfolio exits (batteries, UACJ, copper subsidiary) are completed and the proceeds fund the build without further leverage.
scenario_narratives.bear: A hyperscaler capex digestion from FY2029 repeats the 2001 optical bust for a company that has just committed JPY 150bn of capex to the cycle: revenue falls 6% and 2% in years 3-4, copper retreats, Automotive Systems margins keep falling under Chinese competition and USMCA tariff changes, and EBITDA margin reverts to 8% -- above the 10-year average but, with D&A now 4.2-4.6% of sales on the enlarged asset base, an operating margin of only ~3.5%. On that path owner FCF covers little more than interest and the JPY 292bn of net debt consumes the enterprise value: the equity is worth close to nothing on an owner-FCF basis, and the balance sheet (net D/E 0.67 and rising) rather than earnings becomes the constraint.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the stock is being valued at a cycle high (FY2026 EBITDA margin 8.2% vs a 10-year average of 6.2%, FY2027 guided 11%) with a 2.6x capex step-up committed into that cycle, roughly three-quarters of guided operating profit depends on hyperscaler data-center spending, net debt rose JPY 45bn in one quarter, and the company's own history (2001 OFS acquisition) shows what a digestion phase does to it. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires management's Vision 2030 to be delivered in full (OP 250bn, four times FY2026), which needs the AI build-out, copper, FX and capacity execution all to hold simultaneously. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Furukawa Electric is a cyclical cable and optical-fiber manufacturer whose profits have quadrupled on the AI data-center build-out and a 31% rise in copper prices. The house model values the owner free cash flow that survives the JPY 150bn capex programme and working-capital build, charges leases, NCI and a JPY-built 8.5% WACC once, and credits roughly half of management's Vision 2030 target in the base case. Because reported FCF has been negative in most of the last twelve years and the FY2027-FY2028 cash flows are consumed by capex, nearly all of the value is terminal, and the bear case -- a reversion to prior-cycle margins on an enlarged, debt-funded asset base -- leaves little equity value. The market price implies the bull case (Vision 2030 delivered) capitalised at a full multiple; the base case does not support it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hyperscaler capex digestion in 2028-2030 removing the demand the FY2027 capex programme is built for (the 2001 OFS precedent)

Mid-cycle margin judgment: terminal EBITDA of 10.5% is above anything the company earned before FY2025; if the data-center mix shift is not structural the base case is too high, and if Vision 2030 is delivered it is too low
Copper price (JPY 2,227/kg assumed) and USD/JPY 160 both embedded in guidance; a reversal cuts revenue and working-capital-driven cash flow together

Capex and working capital: FY2027 owner FCF is about -JPY 65bn and net D/E is 0.67 and rising; a second year at 150bn capex or a slower sell-through of new capacity pushes leverage up before the cash returns
Terminal-value dependence: >70% of enterprise value is terminal in every scenario; the 14x FCF cap binds, so the value is sensitive to the terminal margin, not the terminal growth rate
Investment-securities bridge item (JPY 116bn after haircut) is estimated from presentation deltas, not an audited line; a 30% haircut instead of 20% is ~JPY 20/share
Middle East resin/transport cost impact explicitly excluded from company guidance; Automotive Systems margin erosion from Chinese competition and USMCA tariff changes
